findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Observed 3 pallets of apples and onions that were host to a swarm of fruit flies. Food was open to pests without cover in the storage area. A spoiled apple was removed from the container, but the fruit flies remained. CORRECTED: PIC moved the apples and onions to where they can be protected: the walk-in cooler. PIC also discarded any spoiled onions and apples. When PIC moved the apples and onions, and entire pallet of rotten bananas was revealed to be underneath, which also had fruit flies. The bananas were completely black and shriveled. PIC discarded the bananas. Inspector also observed that the potatoes in the same area were shriveled. Ensure that food is safe and unadulterated through good storage practices and frequent quality checks.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that the facility was using “food-contact surface” wipes, but had no way to test the effectiveness of the sanitizing solution contained within. The concentration of the sanitizer could not be measured using Inspector’s test strips (Chlorine, quaternary ammonium). PIC did not have any test strips (see Violation #48). CORRECTED: Inspector had PIC make a standard sanitizer solution using bleach and water, which tested between 50-200ppm. Inspector reminder PIC to only use a cap of bleach when making an sanitizer bucket solution, because too much sanitizer is considered toxic. Ensure that chemical sanitizing solutions measure at safe and effective concentrations for food-contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Observed 3 pallets of onions and apples in the storage area that had a swarm of fruit flies on them. PIC was notified, and identified that some of the onions had rotted, which provides harborage to insects. PIC removed the rotten apple and plans to put the onions and apples in the walk-in cooler where they will be better protected from attracting insects. An additional pallet of rotten bananas was also uncovered and discarded. Inspector discussed changing pest control methods to a paid service instead of facility doing their own pest control. Ensure that the premises is free of pests by inspecting frequently for pests, providing suitable pest control methods for different types of pests, and protecting food from pests.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment:
Observed areas where food was exposed to potential contamination due to where it was stored:
(i) onions and apples were stored above large cannisters and below the soda machine lines. CORRECTED: PIC moved the apples and onions to the walk-in cooler.
(ii) Eggs stored in the walk-in cooler were stored next to a dripping fan, where the drips were to be collected in a pan. CORRECTED: PIC moved the eggs farther away from the dripping.
(iii) Unwrapped bread was stored uncovered without protection from above on basement shelves (bread was unwrapped so it would dry out for a recipe). CORRECTED: PIC placed the bread under a plastic cover.
Ensure food is not stored near mechanical or environmental sources of contamination from above, below, or the sides.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.12(A) and (C)-(I) Food Storage, Prohibited Areas. FOOD may not be stored: (A) In locker rooms; (C) In dressing rooms; (D) In garbage rooms; (E) In mechanical rooms; (F) Under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips; (G)Under leaking water lines, including leaking automatic fire sprinkler heads, or under lines on which water has condensed; (H)Under open stairwells; or (I) Under other sources of contamination. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed that the facility does not have test strips for the available sanitizing wipes, which did not test with either Chlorine or quaternary ammonium test strips. CORRECTED: Working test strips for Chlorine were obtained. A separate sanitizer bucket using regular bleach (Chlorine) was prepared and tested. Ensure sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are tested at a frequency to verify proper sanitizing concentrations.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces that are in need of cleaning to prevent accumulation of soil residues:
(i) the walls of all the freezers have a significant accumulation of ice which can fall onto food.
(ii) the gasket edges have an accumulation of black soil residues.
(iii) the filter of the cooking ventilation hood is completely encrusted with grease and soil residues. Inspector discussed changing hood cleaning methods to a paid service instead of facility doing their own hood cleanings, and more often hood cleanings.
Clean these areas with enough frequency to prevent an accumulation of soil residues that can potentially contaminate food.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed that the kitchen and storage areas for the restaurant are cluttered with unnecessary items, making it difficult to clean with enough frequency to prevent an accumulation of soil residues. Please clear the clutter so that the facility can be maintained for better functionality. Keep personal items separate from restaurant items in storage areas.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed personal foods intermixed with food for service in the triple door cooler. Discussed with the staff members that personal foods need to be completely separate from restaurant foods, either in separate sides of the cooler, or all personal foods on the bottom shelves. Ensure separation of items for personal use from items used for service to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
1ST REPEAT:
Inspectors observed ready to eat foods stored below animal proteins in the kitchen’s 3 door cooler, including, but not limited to:
1) shelled eggs over milk
2) ham over tomatoes.
CORRECTED- ready to eat items were moved above raw items. Inspectors provided an handout with pictures reflecting proper storage order. Ensure food is stored in a manner that protects against contamination (top to bottom= ready to eat> washed produce> unwashed produce> eggs > beef > chicken).
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Multiple temperature control for food safety foods were oberved to be without date marking in the triple door cooler in the kitchen. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) placed dates on TCS items used for service. Ensure all TCS foods used for service are date marked to be used or discarded within 7 days. The day of preparation counts as day ONE.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).[P]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the chlorine bleach sanitizing bucket “bleaching out”, meaning the sanitizer concentration exceeded the maximum sanitizing level for a food-contact surface, as specified by manufacturer. CORRECTED: The sanitizer bucket was remade and observed at an appropriate concentration for sanitizing food contact surfaces. Ensure that all sanitizers shall meet the requirements for use on food-contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions). [P]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Observed that employee foods are being stored amongst foods for customers in the walk-in cooler and triple cooler. The personal foods currently stored intermixed with customer foods (including above or directly next to foods) pose the risk of contamination. The inspector suggests designating specific areas inside the coolers for personal storage. For example, the left side of the triple cooler or the bottom shelves in the walk-in cooler could be designated as personal storage. The PIC can choose whichever storage technique will work best for the facility as long as customer foods are being protected from contamination. Ensure that personal foods are always stored separate from customer foods to avoid contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-305.11 Designation. (A) Dressing rooms or dressing areas shall be designated if EMPLOYEES routinely change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed that the employee working food handler training is expired. The certificate posted in the kitchen pass through window expired in September 2022. The PIC was made aware and stated that the employee will be re-taking the certification. They were reminded that all employees who do not have a CFPM certificate must take the food handlers training. Ensure that the required employee renews their food handler certificate by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Observed that the PIC’s allergen awareness training expired in January 2025. The PIC was reminded that someone with an allergen certificate must be present during all hours of operation. Ensure that the PIC renews their allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. Observed several foods in the triple cooler that did not have date marks. The foods without date marks were half & half, cooked meatballs, and roast beef. The PIC stated the roast beef was prepared on 09/10, the cooked meatballs were removed from the freezer yesterday, and the half & half was opened yesterday. The PIC correctly date marked all of the foods during the inspection. Ensure that foods remaining at the facility for longer than 24 hours are date marked to indicate the 7-day maximum. The day the food was prepared/opened is day 1. Removing foods from the freezer does not restart the 7-days; you must continue the count from before the food entered the freezer. The food must be discarded after 7-days. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf)

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Various containers of pizza toppings were observed to not be date marked.  Inspector asked PIC if they were placed into the containers today, but they had been put in there yesterday.  Discussed date marking with PIC.  Ensure all containers of food are date marked if held longer than 24 hours.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.comment: REPEAT #2: No CFM is present in facility. All category 1 facilities must have CFM certificate. Obtain CFM certificate. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Observed handwashing sink blocked by bucket. Ensure handwashing station is always accessible. Corrected. Bucket has been moved. Education provided. Reference 5-205.11.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: Observed personal items stored above consumer foods. Ensure personal items are placed away/below foods being sold to consumers. Reference 3-307.11.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment: REPEAT #1: Employee present does not have food handler's license. Ensure all food employees have food handler's training certificate. Obtain certificate. Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: REPEAT #1: No CFM is present in facility. All category 1 facilities are required to have CFM certificate. Obtain CFM certificate.
findings.citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment: Observed employee eating within kitchen area. Ensure designated area is used for eating. Corrected. Education provided.
findings.citation_text: 2-401.11  (C) Employee observed eating in the food preparation area. Provide designated area outside for eating. Reference 2-401.11.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Employee does not have food handler license. All employees handling food must obtain food handler certificate. 
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
1)Observed Time and Temperature and Control for Safety (TCS) food (meat) to be without a date mark. PIC stated food was made yesterday. Label food. 
2) Observed TCS food to be held past seven days. Discard food. 
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed food equipment including pans and pots to be in bad repair. Fix, replace, or discard food equipment as needed to ensure smooth easily cleanable food products are used. 
750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
No FSSMC was present during inspection. All Category I facilities need an adequate amount of FSSMC. A follow-up will occur in 90 days. 
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed multiple utensils and food equpiment including spatula, pans, and pots to be in bad repair. Any utensil must have smooth easily cleanable surfaces. Replace any damaged food equipment as needed. 
750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed soda nozzle to be soiled with black debris. All food-contact surfaces must be clean and free of debris.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Water source safe, hot, and cooled under pressure
findings.comment:
Observed no hot water to be present in facility. For facility to operate, the facility must have hot water. Owner is working on solution to fix today. Follow up will occur in several hours. 
750-1120 Each lavatory shall be provided with hot and cold water tempered by means of a mixing valve or combination faucet.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed multiple types of equipment including ice machine and air conditioner to be collecting water through buckets and dumped down designated drain. A floor drain should be provided to recieve discharge that is properly disposed. 
750-1200 Properly installed trapped floor drains shall be provided in floors that are water-flushed for cleaning or that receive discharge of  water or other fluid waste from equipment, or in areas where pressure spray methods for cleaning equipment are used.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed garlic in oil without a date mark in the three door cooler. Ensure that garlic in oil and other RTE, PHFs are date marked, then used or discarded after 7 days.  Product was date marked during the inspection. 
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the spout of the coca-cola machine to have an excessive accumulation of dried syrup build-up. Ensure that, after the nozzle is removed, the spout is cleaned as well. 
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment: 750-350(c) REPEAT(X3) Observed several areas where large amounts of personal articles including food, equipment, and toxic substances stored are intermingled with food, single service, and equipment used to serve the public in the establishment. Only articles necessary for the operation and maintenance of the food service establishment shall be stored on the premises.  Remove all unnecessary items. Due to the large amount of personal article storage in the facility, the matter will be referred to SCDPH administration for review.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-120(a) Observed food (gravy) stored in the chest freezers up stairs and down stairs to be uncovered. This items were stored to be cooled and frozen for future use. Facility should cover and date mark food stored in cold holding units.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment: 750-1300 Observed a spray bottle of sanitizer with no labeling stored in the 3-compartment sink. A label was provided to correct the violation. All chemicals shall be labeled once removed from the original container shall have a label to ensure safe and appropriate use.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment: 750-350(c) REPEAT(x2): Observed several areas throughout the facility where large amounts of personal articles including food, equipment, and toxic substances stored intermingled with food, food equipment, and single service articles used to serve the general public. Only articles necessary for the operation and maintenance of the food service establishment shall be stored on the premises.  Remove all unnecessary items. Designate areas for storage of personal articles. Due to the large amount of personal article storage on the premises, the matter will be referred to SCDPH administration for review.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-151(a) Observed tomato sauce used for pasta stored in the 3-door reach in cooler in the kitchen to have a date marking label of 3/21. Tomato sauce was removed from the premise to correct the violation. All refrigerated, ready-to-eat, potentially hazardous food held in the facility for longer than 24 hours shall have a date marking label and shall be used or discarded within 7 days.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-120(a), 750-130(c) Observed food including pasta stored on a shelving unit in the basement below an exposed sewage line. Food shall be protected at all times during storage. Cease to store food below the exposed sewer line.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment: 750-530(a) Observed personal drinks stored in prep areas in the kitchen. Personal drinks in to be consumed in prep areas shall have a lid and straw and be stored in a manner that does not potentially contamiante food and food contact surfaces. Store personal drinks below and away from food prep and food storage areas.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment: 750-350(c) REPEAT: Observed several areas throughout the facility where large amounts of personal articles including food, equipment, plants, and toxic substances stored intermingled with food, food equipment, and single service articles used to serve the general public. Only articles necessary for the operation and maintenance of the food service establishment shall be stored on the premises.  Remove all unnecessary items. Due to the large amount of personal article storage on the premises, the matter will be referred to SCDPH administration for review.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-120(a), 750-130(c) Observed a shelving unit storing food and single service items stored under water and sewer lines in the basement. Food shall be protected from contamination at all times during storage. No food shall be stored under water lines or sewage lines.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-650(a) (1) Observed a plastic spatula that had been used to the extent that the food contact surface was no longer smooth and easily cleanable. Rubber spatula was discarded to correct the violation. (2) Observed a cloth used to cover bread on the shelving unit in the upstairs kitchen. Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices. Cease to cover bread with cloth. Provide a smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable material such as wax paper to cover bread.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) Observed the hook and bowl of the large mixer in the kitchen to be soiled with an accumulation of food debris, grease, and flour. Clean and maintain food contact surfaces to prevent cross contamination. Food contact surfaces of food equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment: 750-1060 Observed the condenser in the walk in cooler in the basement to be dripping. Repair leak. All plumbing shall be maintained in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code (77 Ill. Adm. Code 890). Do not store any food under or around this leak.

findings.title: Containers covered, adequate number, insect and rodent proof, emptied at proper intervals, clean
findings.comment: 750-1130(a) Observed a metal pan of grease stored uncovered outside the back door. Garbage and refuse shall be kept in durable easily cleanable, insect-proof, and rodent-proof containers.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1210,750-1220 (1) Observed the walls underneath the prep table storing the meat slicer and behind the three compartment sink to be soiled with food splash. Clean and maintain walls. (2) Observed the ceilings in the basement to be falling into a state of disrepair. Walls and ceilings must be maintained to provide a smooth, easily cleanable surface.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment: 750-350(c) Observed several areas where large amounts of personal articles including food, equipment, plants, and toxic substances stored intermingled with food and equipment used to serve the public in the establishment. Only articles necessary for the operation and maintenance of the food service establishment shall be stored on the premises.  Remove all unnecessary items. Due to the large amount of personal article storage, the matter will be referred to SCDPH administration for review.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
(1) Observed a container of what appears to be powder sugar no label on the shelf next the two door reach in cooler. (2) Observed a container of what appears to be salt with no label on the shelf next to the kitchen door. All bulk powders shall be labeled unless their identity is unmistakeable. Provide a label for the flour and salt containers. 
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
(1) Observed no date marking on the galloon of milk, pizza sauce, pasta, and cream in the two door cooler in the kitchen. (2) Observed no date marking on dough, pizza sauce, or homemade pepper mix in the prep cooler in the kitchen. Management stated that all pizza sauce and pasta had been made on Friday 8/19/16. Additionally, management stated that cream, dough, and homemade pepper mix were prepared on Saturday 8/20/16. All potentially hazardous food held for more than 24 hours shall be date marked to ensure they are discarded within 7 days. 
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed the ice scoop laying on top of the ice machine. Ice scoop should be stored in ice with handle extending out or in a manner that protects the food (ice) contact surface.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
Observed employee chewing gum in the kitchen during inspection. Employee discarded gum to correct the violation. Employees may  not chew gum while working in the kitchen. 
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled with what appeared to be food debris: (1) the door of the prep cooler up front (2) exterior of the silverware organizer stored up front under counter (3) the doors of the reach in prep cooler in the kitchen. 750-800e All non-food contact surfaces shall be properly cleaned.

findings.title: Single service articles not re-used
findings.comment:
(1) Observed garlic stored in a re-used, single service ice cream container. (2) Observed homemade pepper mix stored in a re-used, single service parmesan cheese container. Single service containers shall not be re-used for food storage. Food shall be stored in food grade containers.
750-600 Re-use of single-service articles is prohibited. Do not re-use single service items.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment: Observed multiple random, personal articles stored in food prep and food storage areas including, but not limited to the following: (1) caulking stored on the bottom of a shelving unit with sugar and flour, (2) personal medication (such as cough drops) on a tray next to the prep line, (3) empty jars that management stated were being saved for personal use, and (4) car keys stored in food prep area. Personal articles shall be stored away from food storage and food prep areas.750-1350c Only articles necessary for the operation and maintenance of the food service establishment shall be stored on the premises.  Remove all unnecessary items.750-1350a Food service establishments and all parts of property used in connection with their operation shall be kept free of litter.  Remove all unnecessary items.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Observed no FSSMC upon arrival of inspectors at 11:15 AM. FSSMC arrived on-site at approximately 11:25 AM to correct the violation. A FSSMC shall a be on-site for all food preparation and food handling.
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: The following non food contact surfaces are soiled with dust or food debris: 1) Shelf under prep table 2) top of chest freezer in kitchen 3) side of pizza prep cooler 4) shelf over 3 part sink. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris. Clean the above listed items and maintain clean.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:

750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:

750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Observed the basement to have clutter in the area between food and the workshop. Sort out the basement area and the food area.
750-1350a Food service establishments and all parts of property used in connection with their operation shall be kept free of litter.  Remove all unnecessary items.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed wet white rags stored on counter top at the handsink. Store rags in sanitizing solution in between uses.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Repeat violation: Absence of cover for the  baby tray in the dining area. Cover the baby tray.
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Absence of cover for the baby tray in the front of restaurant. Cover the baby tray.
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed a gap in  the board and wall at the handwashing sink up front. Seal the gap.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Absence of covering to the baby tray that is stored up front . Cover the top of tray with saran wrap.
750-860 The food-contact surfaces of fixed equipment shall also be  protected from contamination.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed a gap in the edge of the hood system and ceiling in the kitchen area. Repair the junction surface between the surfaces.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
